title: Region prefetch affinity leak caused cascading fallback surge — post-incident review
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: On 2025-02-17 a region affinity leak in our route prefetch/KV-warmup subsystem caused a sustained surge of misrouted traffic and automatic fallback to lower-tier model variants. The leak amplified over ~45 minutes, increasing tail latency for affected routes and triggering quota-based throttles in downstream tiers. This review documents detection, root causes, immediate mitigations, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~12% of global requests experienced a route deviation from preferred region during the incident window
Fallback rate to cheaper/compatible model variants increased from baseline 0.4% to 18% at peak
P95 latency for affected routes rose from 120ms to 820ms (hosted API tier)
Customer-facing errors (429/503) increased for 3 enterprise tenants that pin versions to dedicated tiers — mitigated by manual capacity bump
timeline: 2025-02-17T10:02Z — First KV-prefetch anomaly alert: increased prefetch queue time on region-us-west-2 router (SLO alert)
2025-02-17T10:07Z — Routing controller observed drift in region affinity score for node-group A; initial automated remediation attempted (soft-decommission) and failed to converge
2025-02-17T10:12Z — On-call engaged (Liam Chen). Rapid spike in fallback metric observed; early mitigation toggled fallback cooldown to 30s
2025-02-17T10:25Z — Fallback surge continued as prefetched KV tombstones were not expiring; manual rollback of recent prefetch logic deployed from main branch
2025-02-17T10:35Z — Short-term mitigation: disabled aggressive prefetch heuristics and reenabled strict affinity enforcement for affected region
2025-02-17T10:47Z — Request routing stabilized; gradual decline in fallback rate observed over next 20 minutes
2025-02-17T11:10Z — Post-incident conference call; decision to run full canary of prefetch change with telemetry gating
root_cause: A recent optimization to prefetch KV entries (PR #1428) introduced a stale-affinity propagation path: when a node served a prefetched prefix, it marked locality affinity as warm without validating node liveness metadata
Affinity warm marks were persisted in a fast-path cache with TTLs managed by a background sweeper that miscomputed tombstone expiry under high queue pressure

When the sweeper under-evicted entries, region affinity state became sticky. The routing plane respected the sticky state and routed traffic toward region slices that no longer had real capacity, causing local overload and triggering downstream fallback policies

Fallback escalation logic is aggressive by design for degraded regions; combined with sticky affinity this produced a positive feedback loop (more fallbacks -> different capacity signals -> more affinity drift)
Insufficient end-to-end invariants between the prefetch cache and the routing controller allowed stale metadata to influence routing decisions for several minutes
detection: We detected the incident via a combination of SLO alerts (prefetch queue time) and a custom fallback-rate alert. The prefetch queue alert fired first; correlation with routing telemetry was added in the post-incident hunt to speed future triage.
mitigations_applied: Rolled back PR #1428 within 13 minutes of detection
Disabled aggressive prefetch mode across affected regions
Temporarily lowered fallback aggressiveness (increased cooldown and required error thresholds for fallback triggers)
Repaired sweeper TTL computation and forced full cache eviction on affected nodes
Scaled up dedicated capacity for three enterprise tenants to absorb transient error traffic (manual commit)
long_term_actions: Add a routing invariant test that fails if cached affinity points at nodes without recent heartbeat (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2025-03-10)
Introduce end-to-end TTL watermarking: prefetch cache entries must include generation tokens validated by the routing controller (owner: Runtime Team, due: 2025-04-01)
Implement telemetry gating: prefetch canary changes must remain disabled unless no-affinity-drift alert is green for 24h (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2025-03-05)
Revise fallback policy to require sustained capacity signals across 2 distinct control-plane cycles before escalating variant switchover (owner: Routing SRE, due: 2025-03-20)
Create dashboard combining prefetch queue, affinity churn, and fallback rate for rapid correlation (owner: Observability, due: 2025-03-03)
Backfill synthetic tests that exercise region drain scenarios including prefetch tombstone generation (owner: Test Engineering, due: 2025-03-17)
notes: Decision: prefer conservative prefetch behavior by default; make aggressive prefetch opt-in per-traffic-class
Trade-off: reduced prefetch aggressiveness will slightly increase cold-start P95 for a subset of requests but significantly lowers routing instability risk
We will not change customer fallback defaults for enterprise tenants in the short term; instead, focus on routing invariants to avoid misrouting
Operational note: add a small synthetic canary in each region that exercises prefetch eviction to ensure sweeper correctness post-deploy
